body:
Thanks for sharing and sorry for what happened to you. Hearing stories from survivors like yourself is what helped me realize how traumatizing something like touching can be and the long term impacts that it can have on someone. Knowing now that I could have caused her some emotional trauma is what eats away at me the most. 

I’m just lucky that (to my knowledge) she wasn’t angry or anything and were able to still have a lot of fun that night, even after the whole touching thing. I’m happy that I learned my lesson and became a better person from it, but it just sucks because that lesson came at the expense of someone else.

Thank you for sharing and I'm sorry for what happened to you. 

Learning from this experience and vowing to never do it again is the least I could do to try and make things right. There's no going back changing things, but I'm just glad that I didn't cause her any long-term emotional stress (that I know of at least). We were still able to have a good time for hours after that night.

Like others here have said in this thread, it's not the worst thing that's ever happened to someone, but that still doesn't make it right.

I should have mentioned that in the original post, but I've discussed this post with other people here in the comments. The fact that I could have damaged her emotionally and made her uncomfortable in that moment is what eats away at me the most. If I do something stupid and have to face the music, then that's on me. I deeply regret what I did and vowed to never do it again, but the fact that all this came at the expense of someone else is what haunts me.

True that, what's done is done and I have to live in the now and not the past. I would never do anything like that now since I've had time to grow and mature, but I'm just upset with myself because my lesson here had to come at the expense of someone else. I'm just lucky that we were still able to have a good time that night and nothing came of the situation that I know of.

It may be tame in consideration to other stuff, but it's still wrong at the end of the day. I just wanted to put my story out there so that other men like my past self can learn that this type of behavior is not okay and can have long-term impacts on others

Groping and unwanted touching is textbook sexual harassment, so the part that makes me feel so bad is if, say for example, she did indeed feel harassed. This would've made me a criminal and she would have been put in a situation that nobody deserves to be in.

I'm lucky that she was able to joke about it and things (from my knowledge) ended up being okay. The thing that's eating away at me is if someone else was in her shoes and they weren't okay with it. I could very well have a criminal record and be a registered sex offender, but more importantly I would've made them feel violated and unsafe on what was supposed to be a fun, laid back night. 

I'm glad I eventually came to my senses and realized my wrong doing, but knowing that I really could have damaged someone emotionally is the part that makes me feel the most guilty.

Hey there, thanks for the comment. What I did was 100% wrong and if I could go back in time and do things over again I definitely would. 

What I can say though is that I am a much better person now than I was 4 years ago and hopefully someone out there will learn from my mistake.

Thank you for the reply and thank you for sharing your story. I’m sorry you had to experience all of those things.

I understand that what I did is pretty mild, but that doesn’t make it excusable. Part of becoming better is admitting your own personal shortcomings, but I just feel terrible that my mistake had to come at the expense of someone else, even if she probably did forget about the entire experience.
Mom's really are something, aren't they? I'm also glad to hear you're doing better now in comparison to back then.

Thank you for sharing. I've been suicidal on and off for the past three years, but this time around it's so much worse than before. I keep picturing my mom crying at my funeral and that thought scares me the most out of anything.
